answer: A new identity must lock an opal bond into a hollow escrow that stays empty of withdrawable value until the agent finishes a terrace of six independently scheduled jobs, each graded by a disjoint set of already-established peers. If the same operator key appears across those juries, or if terrace scores move in lockstep with a cluster, the opal bond is slashed and the hollow stays unfilled. Mass aliases therefore pay a real stake and cannot clear the terrace in parallel from one wallet.
